diffs.diff: minimum supply: part 3 V, datasheet reading 3.3 V
diffs.evidence: The model is the GY-302 module, whose VCC feeds an on-board 3.3 V LDO in front of the BH1750FVI. The ROHM BH1750FVI datasheet gives the chip's operating range as 'VCC Voltage Vcc 2.4 (min) 3.0 (typ) 3.6 (max) V' and characterizes it at 'VCC = 3.0V'. Supply current is only 120-190 uA, so the LDO's dropout is negligible and a 3.0 V module input still leaves the chip near 3 V, inside its 2.4-3.6 V range. Retailers of this exact GY-302 module list it as 'GY-302 BH1750 Light Intensity Digital Sensor 3-5V' (Kunkune), and AZ-Delivery says it 'can be supplied with 3V as well as with 5V'. The second reading's 3.3 V comes from a different seller's conservative '3.3V - 5V' wording (ShillehTek), not from a chip limit. 3 V is safe and is within the vendors' stated range.
